Rashi on Shabbat 122b:10:1.english: One may remove - [This] implies [that] one may remove them on Shabbat from the detachment of their hinge.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:10:2.english: A coop - A structure made for chickens.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:10:3.hebrew: לא נוטלין ולא מחזירין - כדמפרש ואזיל, חזרתו בנין ממש הוא, וסילוקו סתירה גמורה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:10:3.english: One may neither remove nor restore [it] - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain, restoring it is actual building, and removing it is complete demolition.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:11:1.english: What does he hold - That he permits removing it and forbids returning it.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:12:1.hebrew: אי קסבר יש בנין בכלים - וחזרתו בנין, על כרחיך אם יש בנין יש סתירה, ואמאי נוטלין:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:12:1.english: If he holds there is building in vessels - and returning it [is considered] building, perforce if there is building there is dismantling; so why may one remove [it]?

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:13:1.hebrew: ושניטלו קאמר - וה"ק: דלת של תיבה, שידה ומגדל שניטלו, אין מחזירין:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:13:1.english: And it is saying [that they] were removed - And this is what it is saying: A door of a chest, a box, or a closet that was removed, one may not restore [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:1.hebrew: מאי אבל - כיון דלא תנא נוטלין, לא שייך למיתני אבל:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "but" - Since it did not teach "one may remove," it is not appropriate to teach "but."

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:2.hebrew: לעולם קסבר אין סתירה ואין בנין - הלכך נוטלין, ומיהו אין מחזירין מדרבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:2.english: In truth, he holds there is no [prohibition of] dismantling and no [prohibition of] building - Therefore, one may remove [them]; however, one may not restore [them] by rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:3.hebrew: גזירה שמא יתקע - בחזקה בסכין ויתדות, והוה ליה גמר מלאכה, וחייב משום מכה בפטיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:14:3.english: A decree lest one fix [it] - firmly with a knife and pegs, and it would be the completion of work, and he would be liable on account of striking with a hammer.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:15:1.hebrew: קורנס של אגוזים - המיוחד לפציעת אגוזים הוא דקתני מתניתין דנוטלין אותו למלאכתו, משום דעיקרו למלאכת היתר:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:15:1.english: A mallet for nuts - It is [a mallet] designated for cracking nuts that the Mishnah teaches one may take for its work, because its primary [purpose] is for permitted work.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:15:2.english: But [that] of blacksmiths - Since its primary [use] is for forbidden labor, no.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:16:1.hebrew: לצורך גופו - שגופו צריך עוד למלאכה אחרת של היתר, אין מטלטלין אותו לאותה מלאכה, וכ"ש אם אין צריך לגופו אלא לפנות מקומו, דאין מטלטלין:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:16:1.english: For the purpose of [using] it itself - [Meaning] that [the object] itself is additionally needed for another, permitted task, we may not move it for that task; and all the more so if [one] does not need it itself, [but] only to clear its place, that we may not move [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:17:1.hebrew: מי מייחדי לקטן - בשלמא כולהו הני דמתניתין איכא לאוקמא בעשויין ומיוחדין לכך, בר מהני דליכא דעביד להו להכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:17:1.english: Are they designated for a child - Granted, all these [other utensils] of the Mishnah can be interpreted as [referring to ones] made and designated for that [purpose], except for these, since there is no one who makes them for that [purpose].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:1:1.hebrew: אדעתא דרובא - הלכך, ישראל עיקר. ומחצה על מחצה נמי, ליכא למיקם עלה דמלתא, דאיכא למימר עיקר דעתיה דמדליק בשביל ישראל, ואיכא למימר עיקר דעתיה דמדליק בשביל נכרי. אבל נכרי וישראל, והמדליק עצמו משתמש לאורה, ודאי עיקר אדעתא דידיה עביד, וכיון דנר לאחד נר למאה, שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:1:1.english: With the majority in mind - Therefore, the Jew is the primary [beneficiary]. And in [a case of] half and half as well, it is impossible to ascertain the matter, for one can say the primary intent of the one kindling is for the Jew, and one can say the primary intent of the one kindling is for the gentile. However, [if there are] a gentile and a Jew, and the one kindling uses its light himself, he certainly acts primarily for himself; and since a lamp for one [is] a lamp for a hundred, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:2:2.english: That he brought a document - That one who kindled it.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:4:1.hebrew: כל הכלים ניטלין בשבת ודלתותיהן עמהם - כל הכלים שיש להם דלתות, כגון שידה, תיבה ומגדל, ניטלין בשבת, ודלתות שיש להם בצדן עמהן, ניטלין עמהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:4:1.english: All vessels may be moved on Shabbat, and their doors with them - All vessels that have doors, such as a carriage, a chest, or a closet, may be moved on Shabbat, and the doors that they have at their side with them may be moved with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:4:2.hebrew: ואע"פ שנתפרקו - הדלתות מן הכלים ניטלין, ואין דומין לדלתות הבית שאין ניטלין, לפי שדלתות הבית אינן מן המוכן לטלטל, שאינן כלי; אבל אלו הן כלי אגב אביהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:4:2.english: Even though they were dismantled - [i.e.,] the doors from the vessels, they may be moved, and they are not like the doors of a house, which may not be moved; because the doors of a house are not prepared for moving, since they are not a vessel, whereas these are a vessel by virtue of their parent [vessel].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:2.hebrew: דבילה - מאחר שעשאה עיגול, עבה היא מאד וקשה כגבינה, וצריך קורדום לחותכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:2.english: A cake of figs - Since he made it [into] a round [cake], it is very thick and hard like cheese, and an axe is needed to cut it.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:3.english: And a saw - [It is] like a knife, and it has many notches.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:4.hebrew: לגור בה את הגבינה - לחתכו ולחלקו, לפי שממהרת לחתוך דבר עב:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:4.english: To saw cheese with it - To cut it and divide it, since [the saw] is quick to cut a thick substance.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:5:6.english: To scoop dried figs with it - From the barrels.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:2.hebrew: מלגז - כמין עתר שקורין פורק"א של ברזל, ולו ג' שיניים, ומהפכין בו קש בגורן:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:2.english: A pitchfork - A type of pitchfork called forka [Old French: forche], made of iron, and it has three prongs, and they turn straw with it on the threshing floor.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:3.english: To place on it for a child - Food.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:5.english: A shuttle [karkar] - [In Old French:] raiel [a weaving rod or shuttle].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:6.english: To spear with it - To eat berries and any soft fruit with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:7.english: A hand needle - A small needle with which one sews garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:8.english: And [a needle] of sack makers - A large needle with which they sew sacks.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:6:9.english: To open the door with it - [For] one who lost his key.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:7:1.hebrew: ולא מיבעיא בחול - קא סלקא דעתך, ואע"פ שנתפרקו אבשבת דקתני רישא קאי, ומשמע: אע"פ שנתפרקו היום, מותרים, ולא מיבעיא אם נתפרקו מאמש:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:7:1.english: And [there is] no need [to mention] during the week - [The Gemara] initially assumes [that] "and even though they were dismantled" refers to "on Shabbat" that the first clause teaches, and it implies [that] even though they were dismantled today, they are permitted, and needless to say if they were dismantled yesterday.

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:8:1.hebrew: אדרבה - מאי אע"פ שייך למתני? הא ודאי נתפרקו בשבת, איכא למישרי, משום דכי קדיש יומא הוו מוכנין לטלטל אגב אביהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:8:1.english: On the contrary - What [expression of] "even though" is appropriate to teach? Indeed, [if] they were dismantled on Shabbat, there is [reason] to permit [moving them], because when the day became sanctified [at the onset of Shabbat], they were prepared to be moved together with their parent [vessel].

Rashi on Shabbat 122b:9:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר כו' - ואע"פ לא ארבותא דנתפרקו בשבת קאי, אלא ארבותא דנתפרקו או בחול או בשבת קאי, ולא מיבעיא כשהן מחוברין:
Rashi on Shabbat 122b:9:1.english: This is what [the mishna] is saying, etc. - And [the phrase] "even though" does not refer to the novelty that they came apart on Shabbat; rather, it refers to the novelty that they came apart either on a weekday or on Shabbat, and needless to say [they may be moved] when they are attached.

Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:13:1.hebrew: לעולם קסבר יש בנין בכלים כו' - וכשניטלו מטלטלין קאמר, וה"פ הברייתא: "דלת של שידה תיבה ומגדל ניטלין" — פירוש: מטלטלין כשניטלין; ולא כפירוש הקונטרס, דמפרש "שניטלין" דקתני היינו "שניטלו" קאמר, כלומר כשניטל אין מחזירין אותן — דלא יתכן לפרש כן "ניטלין" דסיפא, אלא לשון טלטול הוא כדפרשתי. ופריך: והא נמי "נוטלין" קתני, ועוד: מאי "אבל לא מחזירין"? דלא שייך למיתני אמילתיה דלא (דמיא) [שייך] כלל למאי דאיירי בה; דמעיקרא קאמר "ניטלין" — שמותר לטלטל ואין בו איסור מוקצה, והדר קאמר "אבל לא מחזירין" — שהוא משום איסור בנין. מאי ענין זה אצל זה? לא שייך כה"ג למיתני "אבל" כלל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:13:1.english: "Actually, he holds that there is [a prohibition against] building with regard to vessels, etc." - And [Abaye] is saying [that] when they were removed, they may be moved. And this is the explanation of the baraita: "A door of a chest, a box, or a closet may be removed [nittalin]" — meaning: they may be moved when they have been removed; and not like the explanation of Rashi, who explains [that] "shenittalin" that is taught means "shenittalu" [that were removed], that is to say, when it has been removed one may not restore them — for it is not plausible to explain "nittalin" in the latter clause in that way; rather, it is an expression of moving [from place to place], as I have explained. And [Rava] asks: Even so, it teaches "one may remove [notelin]"! And furthermore, what is [the meaning of] "but one may not restore [them]"? For it is not appropriate to teach [the word "but"] regarding a matter that is not relevant at all to what it was discussing; for at first it says "nittalin" — that it is permitted to move [it] and there is no prohibition of muktzeh in it — and then it says "but one may not restore [them]," which is due to the prohibition of building. What connection does this have to that? It is not appropriate in such a case to teach "but" at all:

Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:17:1.hebrew: רחת ומלגז מי מייחדי ליה לקטן - ורב יהודה ידע ליה לסיפא, אלא דילמא הוה מוקי לה בשיחדה לכך, ככל הנך דמתניתין. ואם תאמר: והאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל בפרק אלו קשרים (לעיל שבת דף קיג.): "כלי קיואי מותר לטלטל בשבת" — דהיינו לצורך גופו, אע"פ שמלאכתו לאיסור? ואין לומר (דמשמע) דשמואל קאמר ליה וליה לא סבירא ליה; מדבעי מיניה מרב יהודה "כובד עליון וכובד התחתון מהו?", אין ולאו ורפיא בידיה — משמע דס"ל הכי. ועוד, דרב יהודה גופיה בסוף כירה (לעיל שבת ד' מו.) קאמר: "שרגא דמישחא שרי לטלטולי". ואין לומר דמיירי כשייחדו להיתר, כדמוקי רב יהודה הנך דמתני', דהא כלי קיואי לא משמע שייחדו, דאם כן אפילו כובד העליון וכובד תחתון נמי? ויש לומר דלא אסר רב יהודה אלא דומיא דפיצוע אגוזים, שהיא מלאכה גרועה לגבי קורנס שמיוחד למלאכה חשובה; וכן כל הנך דמתניתין הוה אסור בלא ייחוד, דמלאכת היתר שלהן מלאכה גרועה היא לגבי הנך כלים שמיוחדין למלאכה חשובה. אבל כלי קיואי ושרגא דמישחא מותר לטלטל לצורך גופן, דמלאכה שלהן חשובה יותר מפיצוע אגוזים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:17:1.english: Are a winnowing shovel and a pitchfork designated for a child? - Now, Rav Yehuda knew the latter clause [of the mishna], only perhaps he would have interpreted it as referring to [a case] where one designated it for that [purpose], like all those [other utensils] of the mishna. And if you say: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Kesharim (above, Shabbat 113a): "A weaver's tools may be moved on Shabbat," which means for the purpose of [using] the object itself, even though its [primary] function is for a prohibited [use]? And one cannot say (that it implies) that Shmuel said it, while he [himself, Rav Yehuda,] does not hold [this view]; [for] from the fact that when they asked Rav Yehuda, "What is [the law regarding] the upper beam and the lower beam?" [he answered] "Yes and no," and it was uncertain in his hand — this implies that he holds this [view]. Furthermore, Rav Yehuda himself at the end of [the chapter entitled] Keirah (above, Shabbat 46a) says: "An oil lamp is permitted to be moved." And one cannot say that it is speaking of [a case] where he designated it for a permitted [use], just as Rav Yehuda interprets those [utensils] of the mishna, for [regarding] weaver's tools it does not imply that he designated them — for if so, [it would apply] even [to] the upper beam and the lower beam as well? And one can say that Rav Yehuda prohibited [moving a utensil whose primary function is prohibited for the purpose of using the object itself] only [for uses] similar to cracking nuts, which is an inferior task relative to a hammer, which is designated for an important task; and similarly, all those [utensils] of the mishna would be prohibited without designation, because their permitted task is an inferior task relative to those utensils, which are designated for an important task. However, weaver's tools and an oil lamp are permitted to be moved for the purpose of [using] the objects themselves, because their [permitted] task is more important than cracking nuts.

Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:2:1.hebrew: אהדרינהו שמואל לאפיה - מיירי שהיה לכל הפחות מחצה על מחצה, דמשום "נר לאחד נר למאה" לא משתריא אלא היכא שהוא ניכר שהוא עושה לצרכו, דתו לא גזרינן אפילו במכירו שמא ירבה בשבילו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:2:1.english: Shmuel turned his face back - [This] refers to a case where there was at least half-and-half [Jews and gentiles]; for on account of [the principle] "a lamp for one [is] a lamp for a hundred," it is not permitted except where it is apparent that he is doing [it] for his own need, for then we do not make a decree, even when he knows him, lest he do more for his sake.

Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:8:1.hebrew: אדרבה בשבת מוכנין אגב אביהן - אע"ג דלקמן בפירקין (שבת דף קכד:) אמר איפכא גבי שברי כלי חרס, דשרי לטלטל יותר כשנשברו בע"ש משנשברו בשבת — לא דמיא, דהכא אכתי כלי הוא, שעדיין עומד למלאכה ראשונה וראוי להתחבר הכיסוי עם הכלי. אבל לקמן לא חשיב כלי אלא מחמת שעומד למלאכה אחרת, הלכך כשנשבר בשבת אסור טפי דהוי נולד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:8:1.english: On the contrary, on Shabbat they are prepared by virtue of their parent [vessel] - Even though later in our chapter (Shabbat 124b) [the Gemara] says the opposite regarding shards of an earthenware vessel, that it is more permitted to move [them] when they broke on Shabbat eve than when they broke on Shabbat — it is not comparable, for here it is still a vessel, as it still stands for [its] original function and the cover is fit to be attached to the vessel. Whereas later, it is only considered a vessel because it stands for another function; therefore, when it breaks on Shabbat it is more forbidden, for it is nolad.

Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:9:1.hebrew: כל הכלים הניטלין בשבת דלתותיהן עמהם - גרסינן, ול"ג "כל הכלים ניטלין", דטובא איכא דאין ניטלין, כגון מסר הגדול ויתד של מחרישה דאפילו ר"ש מודה, כדאיתא בשילהי מכילתין (דף קנז.), וכגון תלתא בת תרי כורי דאסר רבה בשילהי במה מדליקין (שבת דף לה.), וכן חצוצרות לרבי יהודה ונר ישן. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 122b:9:1.english: "All vessels that may be moved on Shabbat, their doors [may be moved] with them" - We read [this version of the text], and we do not read "All vessels may be moved," for there are many [vessels] that may not be moved — such as a large saw and the peg of a plow, regarding which even Rabbi Shimon agrees, as stated at the end of our tractate (157a); and such as a wicker vessel [talta] holding two kor, which Rabbah prohibited at the end of [chapter] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 35a); and likewise trumpets according to Rabbi Yehudah, and an old lamp. [From] my teacher.
